object_description: scaffolding-like structure with a greened ornamental facade wall
design_condition: the building keeps its footprint set by the internal spatial logic, activating the park-facing head end with an outdoor canteen area and a step system towards the street

positive: The designers cleverly responded to the wish for flexible use of the childcare rooms as potential classrooms
The classroom floor plan structure is organised logically without reducing spatial qualities
Unobstructed access is ensured and the function of the main access is strengthened
The revision shows a more generous front zone with fewer stairs and ramps
Larger, partly covered recreation and movement areas are gained
Activating the park side at the head end with an outdoor canteen area is welcomed in principle
It has been solved more consistently with a step system facing the street
The ornamental wall for facade greening, with plants weaving into a lively tapestry, is atmospherically presented
The analogy to industrial scaffolding has proved its worth
The chosen structure can respond to the requirements and be converted into an atmospheric and flexible school space
The project was developed with great care
negative: The footprint could not be reduced, so questions about the outdoor space remain only partially answered
The spaciousness is achieved by moving the fenced kindergarten area into the park perimeter, which was critically questioned
The suggested stone slab paths to the park lack the desired spaciousness and appropriate scale
The greening success and maintenance of the ornamental facade wall are difficult to evaluate
The project suffers from a lack of clarity in dealing with the required open spaces
